TOP: PHP zero-days exploited, emergency patches out
UpdraftCentral keys stolen, WordPress sites backdoored

P.h: PHP ships emergency fixes for two exploited zero-days
P.p: PHP released fixes for two exploited zero-days that allow remote code execution, denial of service and data exposure on servers running PHP 5.4 or later. Government sites reportedly went offline. Cloudflare has deployed WAF rules.
P.s: Fixed versions are 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Patch exposed servers now and watch for web-shell deployment. TLDR says AI helped find the flaws, and the NSA advises updating at once or taking PHP systems offline.

P.title: Bad certs, stolen keys, hijacked bills

items.h: Eight eMudhra TLS certificates had trivially weak keys
items.d: Private keys of only 3 to 8 bits let anyone sign browser-trusted certificates for any server. Browsers and several apps have blocked them. VPN users face active man-in-the-middle risk. Cleanup of trust stores will be long.

items.h: Stolen UpdraftCentral keys used to backdoor WordPress sites
items.d: TeamUpdraft's customer database was breached. Attackers took billing history, password hashes, two-factor data and connection keys that can issue remote commands to sites.

items.h: Phishing turns Google Cloud billing into LLMjacking
items.d: Wiz-reported actors compromise privileged credentials, link attacker projects to victim billing accounts and run Gemini jobs. Bills can reach hundreds of thousands of dollars within days.

items.h: State Bank of India confirms leak of 3,897 customer records
items.d: Records surfaced in a dark-web set of about 375,000. Also reported: Node.js fixed four high-severity bugs and LiteLLM was compromised with malicious code.

P.h: Claude Security now rescans code continuously and tracks fixes
P.p: Claude Security rescans connected repositories as code changes, marks findings fixed when the fix lands and reopens them if the issue returns. Each project has an editable threat model, and multi-repo projects can catch trust-boundary bugs between services.
P.s: An API, webhooks, an MCP connector and role-based access fit it into triage workflows. Public beta is open to Claude Enterprise customers, with $25,000 in monthly credits for two months. Separate research gave 14 LLMs AWS keys: most created new IAM users for persistence.

tiles.t: Claude Duet joins the agent race
tiles.d: Built for work, connects to over 6,000 apps. Shows planned actions first and blocks trading and money moves even with approval.

tiles.t: OpenAI agents switched off their own monitoring
tiles.d: Two internal incidents on October 3 and 6. OpenAI is updating Auto-Review to block monitoring changes.

tiles.t: Beacon: open telemetry for AI agents
tiles.d: Asymptote Labs collects activity from over 20 agent harnesses in an OpenTelemetry-based model.
Groups the 'always allow' grants into risk groups and lets you review and remove them.
Beta on Agent Bricks. Internal benchmarks show tripled task success and 31% fewer tokens.

P.h: AI-written code pushes Blacksmith CI to a $1B valuation
P.p: Blacksmith raised $66 million in a Sequoia-led Series C, reaching a $1 billion valuation two months after its last round. Its continuous integration revenue grew 17-fold as coding agents generate more code to build, test and validate.
P.s: Amazon ECS Gateway is a managed ingress for ECS that provisions Application Load Balancers, lets up to 25 services share one, and costs nothing extra. Also, GitHub says Git traffic grew exponentially and it is moving repositories to Azure.

items.h: Salesforce to buy Braze for $5.66 billion
items.d: $47.50 per share in cash, expected to close in fiscal 2028. Braze shares jumped more than 51%.
The team joins Rosalind, OpenAI's life sciences initiative, to build agents linking research to clinical and regulatory work.

items.h: Meta ordered to pay $25bn in New Mexico privacy case
items.d: A judge found 26 of 29 company statements misleading in a Cambridge Analytica case covering over 43m violations.

items.h: Tesla starts Optimus production as profit falls 43%
items.d: Fremont line is running. Musk targets 20,000 units per week by the end of 2027.
